question: The two isotopic forms of chlorine, with masses 35 u and 37 u, are found in which of the following ratios in nature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**4) 3 : 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chlorine has two stable isotopes: Chlorine-35 and Chlorine-37.
 
• The natural abundance of Chlorine-35 is approximately 75.77%.
 
• The natural abundance of Chlorine-37 is approximately 24.23%.
 
• This results in a ratio of approximately 3:1 for Chlorine-35 to Chlorine-37 in nature.
 
• This ratio affects the atomic mass of chlorine, which is averaged to around 35.5 u.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isotopes:**

 
 
• Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.
 
• Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• The weighted average mass of the atoms in a naturally occurring element.
 
• Calculated based on the relative abundance of each isotope.
 
 
 
• **Mass Spectrometry:**
 
 
• A technique used to measure the mass-to-charge ratio of ions.
 
• Helps in determining the isotopic composition of an element.
 
 
 
• **Chlorine:**
 
 
• A halogen element with atomic number 17.
 
• Commonly found in nature as part of compounds, such as sodium chloride (table salt).
